In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no one scoring system has emerged as the best method to predict mortality for patients with cancer in the intensive care setting.
the use of mortality scoring systems to predict the outcome of critically ill patients with cancer has not been validated.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of critical illness scoring systems to predict the outcome of critically ill patients with cancer is not reliable, and the best predictor of outcome remains a clinical assessment of the patient.
the best approach to triage of the critically ill patient with cancer is to use the same clinical assessment tools and criteria as are applied to all other critically ill patients.
the best approach to triage critically ill patients with cancer involves a systematic assessment of the severity of the acute illness and the likelihood of survival from the current cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a prognostication tool in patients with cancer is not useful for determining who is appropriate for ICU admission.
there are no good tools to prognosticate for patients with cancer in critical care.
there is a lack of data to support the use or nonuse of critical care resources in patients with cancer.
